title: NumPy
label: NumPy
desc: N-dimensional arrays with vectorized math, broadcasting and linear algebra.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install the package and confirm which build is active.

snippets.code:
# Install from PyPI
pip install numpy

# Or from conda-forge
conda install -c conda-forge numpy

import numpy as np

print(np.__version__)   # 2.1.3
np.show_config()        # BLAS/LAPACK backend in use

sections.title: Arrays
sections.description: The ndarray holds one typed block of memory plus its shape.

snippets.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
print(a)          # [1 2 3 4]
print(a.ndim)     # 1
print(a.shape)    # (4,)
print(a.size)     # 4
print(a.dtype)    # int64
print(a.itemsize) # 8
print(a.nbytes)   # 32

# Rows are days, columns are prices for three products
prices = np.array([[10.5, 11.0, 9.75],
                   [12.0, 12.5, 13.0]])
print(prices.shape)                 # (2, 3)
print(prices.strides)               # (24, 8)
print(prices.T.shape)               # (3, 2)
print(prices.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS']) # True

sections.title: Creating Arrays
sections.description: Build arrays from constants, ranges or an existing template.

snippets.code:
np.zeros((2, 3))              # 2x3 of 0.0
np.ones(3, dtype=np.int32)    # [1 1 1]
np.full((2, 2), 7)            # [[7 7] [7 7]]
np.eye(3)                     # 3x3 identity
np.empty((2, 2))              # uninitialized values

np.arange(0, 10, 2)      # [0 2 4 6 8]
np.linspace(0, 1, 5)     # [0.   0.25 0.5  0.75 1.  ]
np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)

# Match the shape and dtype of another array
template = np.zeros((4, 2), dtype=np.float32)
np.ones_like(template)   # (4, 2) float32
np.zeros_like(template)

sections.title: Indexing
sections.description: Reach single elements, positions from a list, or every element matching a mask.

snippets.code:
a = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50])
mask = a > 25
mask                # [False False  True  True  True]
a[mask]             # [30 40 50]
np.where(a > 25, a, 0)  # [ 0  0 30 40 50]
np.nonzero(mask)        # (array([2, 3, 4]),)

grid = np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
grid[1, 2]      # 6
grid[0]         # first row
grid[:, 1]      # second column
rows = np.array([0, 2])
cols = np.array([1, 3])
grid[rows, cols]     # [ 1 11]  one element per pair
grid[[0, 2]][:, [1, 3]]  # 2x2 submatrix

sections.title: Slicing
sections.description: Select ranges per axis; the result is usually a view, not a copy.

snippets.code:
m = np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
m[0:2, 1:3]   # rows 0-1, columns 1-2
m[:, ::2]     # every other column
m[::2, ::-1]  # alternate rows, columns reversed
m[..., -1]    # last column of every row

# A basic slice shares memory with the original
a = np.arange(6)
view = a[1:4]
view[0] = 99
print(a)              # [ 0 99  2  3  4  5]
print(view.base is a) # True

# .copy() detaches the buffer
safe = a[1:4].copy()
safe[0] = -1
print(a[1])           # 99

sections.title: Shapes and Reshaping
sections.description: Change how many axes an array has without touching its values.

snippets.code:
a = np.arange(12)
a.reshape(3, 4)
a.reshape(2, -1)             # -1 infers the 6
a.reshape(2, 2, 3)
a.reshape(3, 4).ravel()      # view when possible
a.reshape(3, 4).flatten()    # always a copy

v = np.array([1, 2, 3])
v[:, np.newaxis].shape            # (3, 1)
np.expand_dims(v, axis=0).shape   # (1, 3)
np.squeeze(np.zeros((1, 3, 1))).shape  # (3,)

m = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
m.T.shape              # (3, 2)
np.transpose(m, (1, 0)).shape  # (3, 2)

a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
b = np.array([[5, 6]])
np.concatenate([a, b], axis=0).shape  # (3, 2)
np.vstack([a, b]).shape               # (3, 2)
np.hstack([a, a]).shape               # (2, 4)
np.stack([a, a], axis=0).shape        # (2, 2, 2)
np.split(np.arange(6), 3)             # three arrays of 2

sections.title: Data Types
sections.description: Every array has one element type, and conversions can lose information.

snippets.code:
np.array([1, 2, 3]).dtype              # int64
np.array([1.0, 2.0]).dtype             # float64
np.array([True, False]).dtype          # bool
np.array([1, 2], dtype=np.float32).dtype  # float32
np.array([1, 2], dtype='int8').dtype      # int8

a = np.array([1.7, -2.3, 3.9])
a.astype(np.int64)      # [ 1 -2  3] truncates toward zero
a.astype(np.float32)    # keeps the fraction, less precision
np.float64(2.5).astype(np.int32)  # 2

np.iinfo(np.int32)    # min=-2147483648 max=2147483647
np.finfo(np.float32)  # eps=1.1920929e-07 max=3.4028235e+38
np.result_type(np.int32, np.float32)  # float64

sections.title: Arithmetic
sections.description: Operators apply element by element, and @ performs matrix products.

snippets.code:
A = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
B = np.array([[0, 1], [1, 0]])
A * B          # elementwise: [[0 2] [3 0]]
A @ B          # [[2 1] [4 3]]
np.matmul(A, B)  # same as A @ B
A.dot(B)       # same as A @ B

sections.title: Broadcasting
sections.description: Shapes are aligned from the right and stretched wherever an axis has length 1.

snippets.code:
# Two 1-D arrays do not broadcast into a grid by default
x = np.arange(3)   # (3,)
y = np.arange(4)   # (4,)
(x[:, np.newaxis] * y).shape   # (3, 4)

# Incompatible axes raise instead of guessing
np.zeros((2, 3)) + np.zeros((2,))  # ValueError: (2,3) vs (2,)

sections.title: Universal Functions
sections.description: Elementwise kernels with reduce, accumulate and outer variants.

snippets.code:
a = np.arange(1, 6)   # [1 2 3 4 5]
np.add.reduce(a)      # 15
np.add.accumulate(a)  # [ 1  3  6 10 15]
np.multiply.outer([1, 2], [10, 20])  # [[10 20] [20 40]]
np.add.at(a, [0, 0, 4], 10)          # a becomes [21 2 3 4 15]

# out= reuses a buffer instead of allocating a new array
a = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
out = np.empty_like(a)
np.exp(a, out=out)
out   # [ 2.71828183  7.3890561  20.08553692]

sections.title: Aggregation
sections.description: Collapse axes into summary values, optionally keeping the dimension.

snippets.code:
a = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
a.sum()          # 21
a.sum(axis=0)    # [5 7 9]   per column
a.sum(axis=1)    # [ 6 15]   per row
a.mean()         # 3.5
a.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True).shape  # (1, 3)

data = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0])
data.sum()        # nan
np.nansum(data)   # 4.0
np.nanmean(data)  # 2.0
np.isnan(data)    # [False  True False]

sections.title: Random
sections.description: Draw samples from a Generator, seeded explicitly for repeatability.

snippets.code:
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)
rng.random(3)                 # 3 floats in [0, 1)
rng.integers(1, 7, size=5)    # 5 dice rolls
rng.normal(loc=0.0, scale=1.0, size=4)
rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0, size=(2, 3))

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
rng.choice([10, 20, 30], size=4, replace=True)
rng.choice(5, size=3, replace=False)  # 3 distinct values from 0 to 4
deck = np.arange(52)
rng.shuffle(deck)
rng.permutation(10)

# The same seed always produces the same stream
a = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=2)
b = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=2)
print(np.array_equal(a, b))   # True

sections.title: Linear Algebra
sections.description: Solve systems, factor matrices and fit least squares.

snippets.code:
A = np.array([[3.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]])
b = np.array([9.0, 8.0])
x = np.linalg.solve(A, b)   # [2. 3.]
np.allclose(A @ x, b)       # True

A = np.array([[3.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]])
np.linalg.inv(A)
np.linalg.det(A)            # 5.000000000000001 (float rounding)
np.linalg.matrix_rank(A)    # 2
np.linalg.norm(np.array([9.0, 8.0]))  # 12.041594578792296
np.trace(A)                 # 5.0

A = np.array([[3.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]])
vals, vecs = np.linalg.eig(A)
U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A)

coef, residuals, rank, sv = np.linalg.lstsq(
    np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]]),
    np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]),
    rcond=None,
)
coef   # [1. 2.]

sections.title: Reading and Writing
sections.description: Persist arrays in the compact binary format or exchange plain text.

snippets.code:
a = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
np.save('matrix.npy', a)
loaded = np.load('matrix.npy')   # exact shape and dtype

np.savez('bundle.npz', first=a, second=a * 2)
bundle = np.load('bundle.npz')
bundle['first']

a = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
np.savetxt('values.csv', a, delimiter=',', fmt='%.2f')
np.loadtxt('values.csv', delimiter=',')   # 2x3 float64

# Header names become fields of a structured array
readings = np.genfromtxt(
    'readings.csv',
    delimiter=',',
    names=True,
    dtype=None,
    encoding='utf-8',
)
readings['temperature']
